questions.prompt: Which work verifies by composition that f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = (x - 3)/2 are inverses?
questions.prompt_markup: Which work verifies by composition that f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = (x - 3)/2 are inverses?

choices.text: f(x) · g(x) = (2x + 3)(x - 3)/2 = 1, so f and g are inverses.
f(g(x)) = 2 · (x - 3)/2 + 3 = x and g(f(x)) = ((2x + 3) - 3)/2 = x, for all real x.
f(1) = 5 and g(5) = 1, so f and g are inverses.
f(g(x)) = 2 · (x - 3)/2 + 3 = x for all real x, and one composition is enough by itself.

questions.correct_answer: f(g(x)) = 2 · (x - 3)/2 + 3 = x and g(f(x)) = ((2x + 3) - 3)/2 = x, for all real x.
questions.grading_note: Both compositions must simplify to x. The others check one composition only, one input only, or multiply the functions instead of composing them.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x² with domain x ≥ 0 and g(x) = √x. Which work verifies that they are inverses and explains why the domain restriction is needed?
questions.prompt_markup: f(x) = x² with domain x ≥ 0 and g(x) = √x. Which work verifies that they are inverses and explains why the domain restriction is needed?

choices.text: The restriction is needed because √x is undefined for x > 0.
f(g(x)) = (√x)² = x for x ≥ 0, and g(f(x)) = √(x²) = |x| = x because x ≥ 0. Without the restriction, √(x²) = |x| ≠ x for x < 0.
f(g(x)) = (√x)² = x and g(f(x)) = √(x²) = x for every real number x, so the two functions are inverses and no domain restriction is needed.
g(f(x)) = √(x²) = ±x, and the restriction chooses the + sign.

questions.correct_answer: f(g(x)) = (√x)² = x for x ≥ 0, and g(f(x)) = √(x²) = |x| = x because x ≥ 0. Without the restriction, √(x²) = |x| ≠ x for x < 0.
questions.grading_note: √(x²) = |x|, which equals x only when x ≥ 0 (for example √((-3)²) = 3). The others ignore |x|, state a false fact about √x, or treat √ as giving two values.

choices.text: f⁻¹(7) = 1/7 because an inverse is a reciprocal, and f(1/7) = 7, so f(f⁻¹(7)) = 7.
f⁻¹(7) = 7 - 3 = 4 by subtracting the outputs, and f(4) = 7 by the pattern.
f⁻¹(7) = 2 because f(2) = 7, and then f(2) = 7, so f(f⁻¹(7)) = 7.
f⁻¹(7) = 3 because f(1) = 3, and then f(3) = 7.

questions.correct_answer: f⁻¹(7) = 2 because f(2) = 7, and then f(2) = 7, so f(f⁻¹(7)) = 7.
